output.title: Anonymise first, automate second
output.body:
Before you automate a portfolio workflow, decide one thing first: will any document that enters the process still contain customer identifiers? If yes, do not feed that file into an AI tool as-is. Mask names, amounts, account numbers, and other identifying details first, then test with the cleaned sample. That is a governance control, not an AI feature, and it stays in the owner’s hands.

For a small business, the useful check is simple. Pick one recurring workflow you already handle in email, CRM, shared drive, or a Zapier/Make step. Trace where the document first leaves your control and where human review happens today. If review already sits in the path, keep it. If the workflow depends on identifiable data, anonymise a sample before you test automation. A tidy input does not make the job magical; it just makes the next decision clearer.

This is not legal advice and it does not remove your compliance obligations. It only reduces exposure before you try AI on the process. If the same workflow still works after masking, you have a cleaner basis for deciding whether automation fits. If it does not, you have found a boundary worth respecting.
